Whether through deliberate restraint or fiscal pressure, the US commitment to European security is likely to shrink by 2035. European NATO members shouldn’t wait to find out by how much. They should be able to defend themselves without Washington, argue Cato’s @JustinTLogan and Rachel Tausendfreund.

ow.ly/ryK450YR3Nu
Cato's “Handbook on Affordability” offers over 100 policy ideas that actually address the root causes, not just the symptoms: cato.org/affordability

Washington's policies aren't solving the affordability crisis — they're fueling it. Here's what would actually work.

Video

AI will undoubtedly disrupt more jobs over time, but comparative advantage doesn’t disappear because AI gets better: when machines do more of certain tasks, humans will shift toward other jobs, and whole new industries will emerge.
Anthropic’s early labor-market evidence finds no increase in unemployment in the most AI-exposed occupations, but slower hiring for younger workers, while overall US unemployment remains at 4.3%.
A basic income’s fiscal cost is high. Even $1,000 monthly payments to every American would cost $3.7 trillion annually — 50% of today’s federal budget.
More modest US universal basic income trials have found recipients worked less and enjoyed more leisure, but showed little evidence of better entrepreneurship or lasting mental-health gains.

It seems fruitless to debate a federally funded ‘universal high income’ idea we cannot currently afford to solve a labor-market apocalypse we haven’t yet seen, explains Cato’s @MrRBourne. 🧵

Reforming federal higher education policy could save taxpayers $200B+ over the next decade. Cato’s @Gillen_Andrew_J outlines a package of changes aimed at reducing waste and improving incentives.

Rising psychiatric diagnoses may say more about a broken incentive system than about Americans' actual mental health. When clinicians are rewarded for diagnosing more, not diagnosing well, the result is runaway spending with no way to measure real outcomes, argues Cato’s Adam Omary.

Learn more: ow.ly/c5mc50YRJHP

Video

In a new @PostOpinions op-ed, Cato’s @mfcannon and former Obama-Biden health advisor Elizabeth Fowler argue that to make health care more affordable, policymakers must address the real driver of rising prices and premiums: the implicit penalties that the federal tax code imposes on workers who want to control their own health insurance decisions. 

ow.ly/RlXW50YROpf

Congress didn’t lose its war powers. It neglected them. Decades of bipartisan deference to presidents have weakened the Founders’ constitutional check — widening the gap between the foreign policy voters want and the one they get, argues Cato’s @brandan_buck.

ow.ly/SJlU50YR5JO

Forget whether Warsh would be “independent.” The real issue is that the Fed has so much discretion at all, says Cato’s @norbertjmichel. Congress should require a monetary policy rule so the Fed's monetary policy is predictable and accountable — not hostage to policymakers' judgment.

ow.ly/PCrZ50YR5rx

“Right to Try” promises hope. But often for terminal patients, a legal right is not the same as access to medicines, which depends on drugmakers, regulators, and review boards moving faster than the disease, explains Cato’s @dr4liberty.

ow.ly/JG4N50YR5kW

New research from North Carolina finds body-worn cameras reduced black incarceration rates by 10.5%. When prosecutors see what actually happened instead of relying solely on police reports, racial disparities in convictions and sentencing shrink, explains Cato’s @jeffreyamiron.

ow.ly/GO3y50YR4Z1
